### Q7UJ86 — CTP synthase
- Organism: Rhodopirellula baltica (strain DSM 10527 / NCIMB 13988 / SH1)
- Reviewed: True
- Source: local_uniprot_swissprot_xml
- Homology: identity=61.1%, query coverage=99.8%, target coverage=96.6%, E-value=3.94e-238
- function: Catalyzes the ATP-dependent amination of UTP to CTP with either L-glutamine or ammonia as the source of nitrogen. Regulates intracellular CTP levels through interactions with the four ribonucleotide triphosphates.
- pathway: Pyrimidine metabolism; CTP biosynthesis via de novo pathway; CTP from UDP: step 2/2.
- subunit: Homotetramer.
- regulation: Allosterically activated by GTP, when glutamine is the substrate; GTP has no effect on the reaction when ammonia is the substrate. entities.name: Query CTP synthase
observations: 531 aa; estimated molecular weight 59.1 kDa; theoretical pI 5.49; predicted net charge at pH 7 is -16.0.
Strong homology to reviewed bacterial CTP synthases: 59.5–61.1% identity over 99.6–99.8% query coverage, E-values 8.1e-232 to 3.9e-238.
Pfam supports an N-terminal CTP synthetase domain (PF06418, residues 2–266) and a C-terminal glutamine amidotransferase class-I domain (PF00117, residues 301–524).
Also matches Peptidase_C26 (PF07722) over residues 363–507; this is consistent with the catalytic glutaminase region but should not by itself imply a protease function.
Most likely catalyzes ATP-dependent conversion of UTP to CTP using glutamine or ammonia as nitrogen source; EC 6.3.4.2 is supported by homolog annotations.
Likely participates in de novo pyrimidine/CTP biosynthesis and is cytosolic; reviewed homologs are homotetramers.

Homolog annotations report GTP activation when glutamine is the nitrogen donor and product CTP allosteric inhibition; these regulatory details are inferred for the query, not directly experimentally demonstrated.
Candidate reactions include glutaminase chemistry, glutamine-dependent CTP synthesis, and ammonia-dependent CTP synthesis; exact substrate preference is not established solely by homology.
